requirements.text: OpenCode session ID must move into provider-native correlation; canonical thread_id must remain PM correlation rather than being conflated with the OpenCode session identifier.

Provider boundary must offer a legal place for rewrite-era correlation and pressure semantics; bridged envelopes must carry actor/role/account/switch/trust signals at the stream layer rather than only in addenda, with provider_attempt_ref? and similar continuity fields owned by stable schema slots.

Permission semantics must reconcile ask/plan -> deny for mutating tools with external_publish_side_effect remaining a non-bypassable ask/approval path so remote side-effect approval cannot diverge by surface or mode.

Permission control must be safe under parallel actors via a canonical scope key; always, reject-cascade, and doom-loop behavior must not rely on vague same-session semantics now that shared-runtime actors, lanes, and accounts make ambiguity a correctness bug.

Permission snapshots must carry requested capability state, downgrade reasons, effective account/operational identity, and actor/surface scope so blocked overlays can explain who/what would have executed the side effect under the final runtime identity model.
Extend the shared effective-resolution/runtime identity model with execution_role, requested_operational_identity?, and effective_operational_identity?.
Operational identity may be displayed alongside provider/account identity but must not be implied to share the same ownership or token source unless the owning auth contract says so.

execution_role must be added to the effective-resolution record, attempt_record, tier_runtime_record (or its successor graph-owned runtime record), and usage_record; operational-identity blocks must be added to runtime records where side-effectful or externally-scoped actions matter.

Add a canonical append-only event/record family for account-pressure and switching, minimally covering account_pressure_episode (pressure state with confidence/source over time) and account_switch_event (actual routing change or failed-switch decision); a single unified family must still carry both pressure cause and switch outcome to avoid ambiguous history.

Keep account_switch_reason on effective/runtime snapshots as the current-run disclosure field while adding append-only switch/pressure history families; Usage, History, Ledger, and Orchestrator must consume the same event family rather than inventing local switch-history views, and signal_confidence and source_kind must be preserved so pressure timelines do not overstate certainty.

Switch/pressure history must support both provider-wide and account-specific views, must not become a second quota system, and must plug into the shared Usage/runtime pipeline; failed or blocked switch decisions remain historically important even when the effective account did not change.

Replace tier-era Dashboard/Orchestrator widget vocabulary with the rewrite-era Progress/Seams set; add a concern-model GUI contract and projection-health/degraded-trust contract to FinalGUISpec.md; add projection-freshness gating and typed route payloads to UI_Command_Catalog.md; extend runtime-artifact envelopes and cost_usage linkage with canonical identity/trust/switch fields or refs; normalize GUI consumers onto canonical persona/account/role naming and stop allowing stale local variants.

Add explicit auth/account/role disclosure sections to assistant and interview runtime contracts; add actor/lane/account identity and approver provenance to HITL request/resolution events; define an Approval Scope Key consistently across permissions, HITL, doom-loop, and session approval caching; extend tool events with node/attempt/actor/account context and reconcile tool outcomes with canonical blocked codes; add thread-level switch/concern/trust surfacing paths rather than leaving them only to Orchestrator pages.

Consolidate Executor_Protocol.md addenda and add package/seam/corroboration/concern hooks; introduce node/actor/lane-aware execution context into orchestrator runtime structs and active-agent tracking; replace or wrap TierContext with a node-native execution context carrying full canonical runtime identity; add explicit CUP governance and handoff fields (execution_role, requested/effective account, isolation/worktree mode) to wizard docs; move worktree docs onto node/lane-aware vocabulary and define projection authority between Source Control and Orchestrator receipt lineage.

Use projection_freshness as the canonical recency field and projection_health as the canonical reliability/usability field; reserve trust_tier for preview/browser semantics; supporting fields include projection_freshness, projection_health, last_projected_at_utc, source_seq? (or equivalent checkpoint/cursor), degraded_reason_code?, and refresh_in_progress?.

Consolidate execution-core docs around a single node-native execution context object that replaces or wraps TierContext and is the canonical handoff between scheduler, worker spawn, verification, remediation, recovery, and UI projections; treat tier language as legacy decomposition/help/view terminology; rewrite Executor_Protocol.md so runtime scheduler remains canonical readiness/transition authority, node execution workers are explicit, package/seam overseers are governance actors (not the scheduler), and reviewer/corroborator/remediation/recovery hooks are first-class execution participants; rewrite orchestrator-subagent-integration.md as a consumer/worker-spawn document over canonical runnable units; move worktree ownership to lane/worktree plus canonical run/node/attempt references.
Minimum canonical execution_unit_context identity fields: project_id, run_id, thread_id?, feature_seam_id?, work_package_id?, node_id, attempt_id, replan_generation.
Minimum execution_unit_context execution/governance fields: execution_role, scheduler_lane, manual_priority?, remediation_root_id?, remediation_parent_attempt_id?, safe_point_id?.
Minimum execution_unit_context workspace/isolation fields: lane_id?, worktree_id?, workspace_path, worktree_path?, snapshot_ref?.

Minimum execution_unit_context requested/effective runtime identity fields: refs or embedded snapshot for canonical requested/effective persona/runtime record, plus requested_account_policy?, requested_account_id?, requested_account_binding?, effective_account_id?, account_switch_reason?, and operational_identity?.
Minimum execution_unit_context runtime-state hooks: blocked_reason_code?, allowed_action_ids[]?, failure_class?, permission_snapshot_id?, model_snapshot_id?, provider_attempt_ref?.
Worker spawn, verification, remediation, recovery, coordination state, history, ledger, receipts, and graph/detail inspectors must all anchor to execution_unit_context, not to decomposition_context.

Define one canonical execution_unit_context owner doc shared between Executor_Protocol.md and Prompt_Pipeline.md and have storage/event/docs consume it by reference; any TierContext replacement must remain at most a compatibility wrapper (legacy_decomposition_context plus canonical execution_unit_context, never the inverse); migrate coordination and crew models from tier_id anchoring to canonical execution refs (run_id, node_id, attempt_id, lane_id?, work_package_id?, feature_seam_id?); treat worktree/lane binding and requested/effective account/runtime identity as mandatory parts of canonical execution context.

decisions.text: Carry forward candidate fixes: move OpenCode session IDs into provider-native correlation fields; add a versioned stream/provider correlation block for actor/attempt/account/trust metadata; reconcile ask/plan and external_publish_side_effect semantics in one canonical algorithm; define an Approval Scope Key spanning actor/lane/run/account context; upgrade permission snapshots to carry requested/effective values, downgrade reasons, and identity context; add explicit versioning/migration notes where A2A or bridged categories/fields must grow.
Recommended execution_role examples: assistant, interviewer, requirements_builder, prd_builder, package_overseer, seam_overseer, node_worker, reviewer, corroborator, recovery_actor.
Recommended operational-identity shape: kind, requested_ref?, effective_ref?, selection_reason?, partial_capability?.
Recommended operational-identity kinds: github_api_account, registry_namespace, kubernetes_context, with future provider/surface-specific kinds added as needed.

If kept as two families: account_pressure_episode tracks pressure state and confidence/source over time, account_switch_event records the actual routing change or failed-switch decision; if kept as one family it must still carry both pressure cause and switch outcome.

Split projection-state into two axes rather than one overloaded trust enum: projection freshness (how up to date), projection health (whether reliable/usable); freshness axis is current | refreshing | stale; health axis is healthy | degraded | unavailable.

Owner map: Contracts_V0.md owns canonical snapshot field names (requested_account_id, requested_account_binding, execution_role, operational-identity snapshot block names) and stable event names for account pressure/switch history and new blocked/recovery/governance event families; storage-plan.md owns concrete record/projection families (project_summary, project_attention_item, account pressure/switch episode records, projection freshness/health fields) plus projector/refresh semantics and fallback rules; Prompt_Pipeline.md owns requested/effective runtime resolution semantics including requested concrete account, requested/effective operational identity, and execution role; Multi-Account.md owns selection policy and role/account precedence rules; UI_Command_Catalog.md keeps stable command IDs aligned with canonical route payload vocabulary owned elsewhere; Glossary.md owns final canonical term definitions for projection freshness/health, project summary, attention item, and operational identity; Executor_Protocol.md and orchestrator-subagent-integration.md need a consolidation pass for node-native execution context and package/seam/corroboration/concern/lane/worktree-aware scheduling.

Replacement for TierContext is not 'TierContext but with more fields' but a split: canonical execution_unit_context for runtime/scheduler/worker/governance/storage/UI inspection plus an optional derived decomposition_context or view_context for legacy prompt heuristics, decomposition labels, or UI help text.

data_shapes.text: account_pressure_episode field: episode_id (record-identity field opening the family).

account_pressure_episode fields: project_id, provider_id, account_id, execution_role?, source_kind, signal_confidence, pressure_kind, projected_remaining?, reset_at?, started_at_utc, updated_at_utc, ended_at_utc?, status (active | cooled_down | resolved | invalidated).

account_switch_event fields: switch_event_id, project_id, provider_id, execution_role?, requested_account_id?, requested_account_binding?, from_account_id?, to_account_id?, switch_reason, decision_kind (switched | stayed | blocked_no_backup | blocked_required_account | failed), source_episode_id?, run_id?, attempt_id?, thread_id?, ts.

Optional derived decomposition_context may carry human-readable labels/titles, former tier grouping (for help or migration), language/domain/framework hints, subtask-focus heuristics, and parent-summary/dependency prompt conveniences.

routing_rules.text: origin must remain audit-only even after actor identity becomes first-class elsewhere; provider continuity may stay opaque only if opacity is explicit and projected as such; blocked/approval truth and account/pressure truth are intertwined and must be fixed together.

execution_role is not the same as run_kind, operational identity is not provider account identity, and effective_project_id is correlation context (not a substitute for operational identity); this seam affects Orchestrator, GitHub Actions, Docker Manager, Usage, History, and Ledger simultaneously.

UI_Command_Catalog.md projection-freshness gating must apply to mutating/recovery commands; cross-surface route/open commands must carry the identity/trust context the ledger now recommends; artifact panels and evidence flows need runtime-trust/provenance fields strong enough to support direct-record fallback.
Action gating must use both freshness and health axes: stale-but-healthy may allow read-only use with warning, while degraded or unavailable should gate mutating actions much more aggressively.

execution_unit_context replacement must inherit existing canonical runtime snapshot contracts (not create a parallel runtime-resolution schema); tier_runtime_record may survive only as a derived grouping/view object if execution ownership moves elsewhere; coordination state is a place where stale tier_id usage will quietly persist unless explicitly migrated.

verification_rules.text: Fields like effective_project_id and receipt refs are useful correlation but do not make requested-vs-effective operational identity visible as first-class runtime truth.

Preview trust_tier and runtime projection trust must stay distinct; artifact provenance/trust must remain valid even when the live worktree or provider session is gone; the Orchestrator/Usage/GitHub deep-link story is blocked more by missing route payload/trust contracts than by missing page chrome.

'Approve for session' is now a correctness bug if not scoped properly; persona display is not a substitute for actor/role identity; DAE runs need a clear post-hoc tool-event story or analytics/blocked truth will drift immediately.

preview/browser trust_tier must not be casually reused as the generic projection-state term; users need both axes (is this data old? is this data trustworthy enough to act on?); current posture favors exact record-backed fallback (History, Ledger, record inspectors) when projection health is degraded.

Execution-core problem is no longer just stale terminology; there is a real split-brain between execution context keys; scheduler addenda are insufficient if top-level docs still teach the old ontology; any reconciliation that touches UI/storage/help without first tightening execution-core ownership will keep reopening the same seams; TierContext replacement/wrapper is one of the most important structural follow-ups still open.

owner_consumer_obligations.text: Highest-risk impacted docs from the provider boundary cluster: Plans/Provider_OpenCode.md (canonical/session identity ownership), Plans/CLI_Bridged_Providers.md (versioned correlation/context block plus account-health semantics), Plans/Provider_Stream_Mapping_External_Reference_A2A.md (stream version governance for actor/account/trust semantics), Plans/Permissions_System.md (scope-keyed approval semantics, richer permission snapshots), and Plans/Contracts_V0.md plus Plans/storage-plan.md (canonical blocked/approval identity linkage and pressure/switch projection families).

GUI inspectors must show requested/effective provider/account identity, requested/effective operational identity, execution role, and selection/switch reason; cross-surface receipt refs remain linkage, not the sole operational-identity disclosure model.

Highest-risk GUI-cluster impacted docs: Plans/FinalGUISpec.md (broadest consumer doc, missing concern/trust/switch/pressure and rewrite-era widget/tab contracts), Plans/UI_Command_Catalog.md (governance families, route-payload normalization, projection-freshness gating), Plans/Runtime_Artifacts_Panel.md (producer identity, trust/provenance, cross-surface linkage), and Plans/Orchestrator_Page.md plus Plans/Widget_System.md (still consume stale tier-era surface assumptions).

Several docs still claim 'no open questions' while their supposed dependencies remain undecided elsewhere; UI_Command_Catalog.md is being used as a de facto navigation contract where a deeper route payload is still unowned; Executor_Protocol.md and orchestrator-subagent-integration.md trail the newer graph/package/seam/lane model enough that downstream docs keep compensating locally.

Before reconciliation, define an explicit owner table for the remaining open contracts so downstream edits do not keep re-litigating field placement; treat orchestration-core consolidation as a prerequisite for any final reconciliation of runtime/UI behavior that depends on execution semantics; stop letting consumer docs fill owner gaps with compatibility fields or local terminology when the canonical owner is undecided.

stale_retirement_items.text: Stale items: OpenCode misuses canonical thread_id for provider-native session identity; bridged contracts cannot legally carry all correlation/account/trust metadata their addenda imply; A2A blocks clean category growth despite rewrite-era semantics needing first-class stream representation; permission mode override semantics conflict on remote side effects; permission approval caching and reject-cascade lack actor/lane/account scope; permission snapshots do not project requested/effective identity richly enough.

Stale GUI surface ownership: Dashboard and Appendix C still center tier/task/subtask widgets and vocabulary; Tiers still survives as a first-class tab where the rewrite now wants seam/package/node surfaces; the 12-widget rewrite-era Progress set still has no concrete home in FinalGUISpec.md.

Runtime artifact contracts thinner than identity model: artifact envelopes still have no producer identity, role, account, or switch lineage; cost_usage does not require a durable usage/switch join key strong enough to back Usage/Ledger deep links; runtime-artifact payload ownership is split across docs without a populated canonical schema family; GUI identity projections still omit account/role/operational-identity/switch-history/trust-state.

Stale orchestrator drift: node-native plan ingest still feeds tier-native execution models; lane-aware scheduling does not flow into worktree and active-agent tracking; concern/corroboration/promotion objects remain absent from core runtime protocols; wizard handoff leaves identity/worktree policy implicit; worktree blocked reasons and historical lineage preservation lack a single clear owner/emitter model; stale 'no change to tier/subtask execution' language still appears in summary tables.

Execution-core split-brain: Executor_Protocol.md presents execution as a canonical Builder/Verifier/Overseer loop over graph nodes while orchestrator-subagent-integration.md still defines runtime machinery around Phase -> Task -> Subtask -> Iteration, TierContext, tier-boundary hooks, tier crews, and tier-keyed worktree identity; WorktreeGitImprovement.md's concrete execution/storage assumptions remain tier-keyed (owner run/tier, get_tier_worktree(tier_id), tier-based branch/worktree naming, Orchestrator consumption naming Tiers tab); execution identity is spread across incompatible keys (node-native run_id/thread_id/node_id/attempt_id/replan_generation/scheduler_lane vs. stale tier_id/TierType/TierContext/tier-level crews/tier worktree ownership).

Stale execution-core contradictions: Executor_Protocol.md still claims canonical execution roles as Builder, Verifier, and Overseer when the rewrite needs runtime scheduler ownership, node execution worker identity, package/seam governance identity, and reviewer/corroborator/remediation/recovery execution hooks; orchestrator-subagent-integration.md still treats Iteration as the lowest execution tier; WorktreeGitImprovement.md's runtime ownership remains tier-first.

TierContext is overloaded, combining decomposition/view identity (tier_type, tier_id, title, description), workspace binding (workspace, worktree_path), project heuristics (language/domain/framework), live execution hints (code-review/testing/error flags), and requested/effective runtime fragments; this mixture is the core reason it cannot become the rewrite-era canonical execution context.

Prompt_Pipeline.md still allows persona_override_owner_id scope values that include tier_id (legacy ownership key) requiring migration toward run/node/attempt/subagent-owned scopes; storage-plan.md still has both attempt_record and tier_runtime_record (acceptable only if tier_runtime_record becomes derived/view-oriented); coordination examples and crew creator payloads still treat tier_id as canonical orchestrator ownership key.

open_questions.text: Open question: without a dedicated operational-identity layer, will later UI surfaces overload provider/account fields incorrectly or invent local one-off displays for GitHub/registry/Kubernetes context?

Open question: should account-pressure history and switch decisions remain two families or be unified, and how should signal_confidence and source_kind be preserved while keeping pressure timelines from overstating certainty?

Open GUI questions: GUI still claims tier/task/subtask surfaces where rewrite-era seam/package/node surfaces are intended; no explicit concern model exists in the primary GUI specification; commands changing execution truth lack a shared stale/degraded-projection gate; artifact envelopes cannot answer who produced them under which identity/trust state; widget/page drill contracts lack typed route payloads tied to canonical identity/trust/linkage.

Open question: what concrete replacement for TierContext should carry canonical execution-unit refs, lane/worktree refs, requested/effective runtime identity, execution role, governance lineage, and remediation/replan generation as a single object?

process_defects.text: account_switch_reason currently does too much work as a single field, conflating pressure cause with switch outcome and collapsing current-state with historical-state concerns; provider_accounts.health is a current-state family rather than durable episode history; notification copy assumes switch outcomes (threshold_preemptive_switch, no eligible backup) without a canonical durable event family behind that assumption.

Conversational/HITL/Tooling defects: docs promise requested/effective runtime truth but omit account/auth details in concrete sections; HITL and permissions still mix tier-boundary governance with tool-level approval semantics; tool events remain under-attributed for node/actor/account-aware audit; approval/blocked records cannot explain which effective account/identity would have executed the action; concern and trust-state escalation lacks a shared conversational/tooling surface contract.

Projection-freshness defects: research wording risks colliding with preview/browser trust_tier; freshness and degradation are often discussed together so later docs could collapse them into one field family by accident; no owner doc yet explicitly defines projection freshness/health fields as a reusable cross-surface contract.

Execution-core defect: doc set still lacks one explicit replacement for TierContext, which is now a primary blocker because multiple seams need the same fields (canonical execution-unit refs, lane/worktree refs, requested/effective runtime identity, execution role, governance lineage, remediation/replan generation).
